chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Abdawayh al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us, saying: Tamim ibn Buhlul narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih ibn Abi Salama al-Nusaybi narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Awana narrated from Abu Basheer, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Aisha, who said:

I was with the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family), and Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) approached and said: 'This is the Master of the Arabs.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, am I not the Master of the Arabs?' He said: 'I am the Master of the sons of Adam, and Ali is the Master of the Arabs.' I said: 'And what is a Master?' He said: 'The one to whom obedience is made obligatory, just as I made obedience to me obligatory.'

key_terms.سَيِّدُ ابْنِ آدَمَ: Master of the sons of Adam

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the Prophet being the Master of the sons of Adam and Ali being the Master of the Arabs?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* highlights the distinct hierarchical status of Imam Ali (AS) as the 'Master of the Arabs,' a title that complements the Prophet’s universal leadership as 'Master of the Sons of Adam.' The definition of 'Sayyid' here as one whose obedience is divinely obligatory (*mafruḍ*) underscores the concept of *Amr Ilahi* (Divine Command), linking political and spiritual authority to the necessity of following the Ahl al-Bayt. This distinction reinforces the Shia doctrine of *Imamah* by establishing Ali’s authority as a specific, obligatory duty for the Arab community, distinct yet connected to the Prophet’s own status.
